Extreme close-up macro still life, shallow depth of field. A slim pink #E07FA8 enamelled needle held upright in the dark, its eye in razor-sharp focus. A single magenta #D8258C silk thread, glossy and slightly frayed at its tip, is sliding slowly into and through the narrow eye of the needle, the thread just pushing out the far side. A warm oil lamp flame just out of frame to the left rakes across the needle's polished side and the twist of the silk. Behind, creamy out-of-focus bokeh of lamp glints and folds of magenta and pink silk in an umber-dark room. Intimate, slow, suggestive. PAINTED STILL — no people, no figures, no faces, no hands anywhere in the frame; the place or object IS the subject. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). Hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL: granulated wet-in-wet washes and broken-colour dabs for sky, water and stone, dry-brush texture, soft bleeding edges and a faint paper grain; oil glazes deepen the darks and a touch of impasto lands on the single brightest highlight. Romantic-painting layout: one bold shape, at least half the frame quiet negative space, distant detail dissolving into haze. Film tenebrism: one hard directional key (sun, moon or lamp) against big dark masses, a thin edge of real light along the subject, painted bokeh from small real lights. Sensual and suggestive by shape and motion alone, never anatomical, never explicit. Beautiful, luminous, painterly. NOT photoreal, NOT 3D, NOT a cartoon. No text. No watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
